rationale: A wins because it keeps its hands cleaner: it names the category, Powerwall counterposition, and public-company strategy without smuggling in market lore the update did not provide. A's strongest line is "A profitable public electronics giant is funding its own move into home energy," which opens a real business-desk lens B never quite matches. B has good bones, but "home battery adoption has been slower than solar's trajectory" and "installation barrier has been cited repeatedly as the main friction point" are unsupported decorations; that is how a decent angle turns into a fact-check problem.
gaps_in_A: The category angle overreaches with "any second consumer-electronics maker making the same move"; that is the right proof request, but it also admits the category thesis is still one-company thin.
"Take on Tesla Powerwall without the rewiring" is useful but a little too binary; the update says Anker says no major rewiring, not that this is proven or meaningfully different from Powerwall.

The next step says `newsjack-detector`; for a launch-angle set, the more immediate next move is to get price, capacity, warranty, installer coverage, and an independent installer read before chasing outside hooks.
gaps_in_B: Invents context in "home battery adoption has been slower than solar's trajectory"; that may be true, but it is not in the supplied update.
Invents context again with "The installation barrier has been cited repeatedly as the main friction point"; unsupported market claims are not seasoning, they are liabilities.
"value-oriented buyers" is not grounded in the update. Anker makes chargers and power banks; the facts do not say its buyers are value-oriented or that this transfers to whole-home batteries.
The next step jumps to `journalist-fit-check` too soon. These angles still need the undisclosed product facts and independent verification before matching reporters.
